newsitem.title: USA: Relief in sight for drenched US Pacific Northwest.
newsitem.headline: Relief in sight for drenched US Pacific Northwest.

text.p: Rains and melting snow continued to drench the U.S. Pacific Northwest on Thursday but cooler, drier weather is expected shortly, meteorologists said.

"Today (Thursday) is the last really severe day. Drier conditions should finally develop on Friday and it should cool off as well, lessening the amount of snow melt," said Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino.

River levels have been climbing in Washington and Oregon due to a combination of melting snow and a further one to three inches of rain during the last couple of days. Northern California has had even heavier rainfall, he added.
Several grain merchandisers in the Portland area said they believed that although rail traffic was moving slowly, grain shipments have been able to reach Pacific Northwest ports.
But one merchandiser said he had heard talk that water was too high at some facilities for grain to be loaded onto ships.
The largest amounts of rain have fallen in the Sierra Nevada mountains with 14 inches around Lake Tahoe during the last 48 hours, Palmerino said.
"We have tremendous flooding conditions. Snow melt is the biggest problem and we have had a heavy amount of rain on top," WSC's Palmerino said.

Temperatures in Washington and Oregon have been in the 50s to mid-60s Fahrenheit but look set to drop to more normal highs in the 30s and 40s F with lows in the 20s and low 30s F on Friday. A high pressure system should also bring dry weather into the region which should continue into next week.
Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express, said after more rain on Thursday, showers should taper off on Friday, and Saturday should be a dry day in the Pacific Northwest region.
He said the drier, cooler weather should last "at least a week."
Gesser noted that during December, rainfall in the area was between 200 and 400 percent of the normal range of 2.5 to 6.5 inches, which in some places represented more than 20 inches for the month.
